detail: Build custom bass drums with a dedicated kick-design plugin, shaping six parameters to get a unique kick sound rather than using a stock kick.
Automate LFO rates on synths so the frequency content keeps evolving across a track instead of sitting static.
Introduce a new chord progression at the end of four- or eight-bar blocks, start sections sparse and layer up to the drop, and never repeat an ending the same way.
Set a vocal clip to Complex warp, extend it, then run Auto Pan at 360 degrees phase and 1/16 rate while automating its amount up to full on a single note for a roomy processed vocal.
When stuck, generate randomized drum tracks in Ableton by feeding the find-similar-sounds feature with pattern ideas and letting it propose variations.
Swap a hi-hat track from one side of the stereo field to the other at chosen points and keep moving elements across the field, so headphone listeners never hear a part parked statically on one side.

Start a remix by downloading the song as a MIDI file and dropping it into the DAW, which loads the full arrangement across tracks, then edit that arrangement into your own version instead of building from scratch.
Set up a vocal pitch-correction plugin at full strength on a custom scale rooted on C with only the sharp notes enabled and smoothing on, tracking the sung pitch in real time.

Isolate the start of a vocal, add heavy reverb with a roughly four-second decay, bounce and reverse it so the tail leads into the dry vocal, then add a tremolo whose rate automates upward for a rising wobbling effect.

Load three single-note samples into separate convolution slots in a synth, drive each slot's mix with its own randomized LFO over a saw wave and pink noise, so the convolvers catch and reverberate the harmonics of whatever is played rather than adding new pitches.

Rescue a flat chord stack by adding reverb and then running it through an auto-filter whose LFO sweeps slowly, duplicating the automation across the clip, adding a touch of drive, and automating the LFO amount in gradually.

Route a saw wave through a dirty filter into a frequency-shifting Bode module, then shape the result with shift offset, delay and feedback for the tail, blur for smearing, and balance panning to bend the tone up or down into tight metallic tails.
Turn any single-hit sample into a playable sustained instrument by dropping it into a sampler, choosing a loop point, and dragging the loop markers to define the sustain region.
Sync lyrics to music and automate text animations directly inside the DAW to produce audio-reactive visuals without leaving the session.

Write a chord progression, duplicate its MIDI with all notes forced to one octave at a 1/8 rate, feed an acapella through a pitch-correction plugin driven by that MIDI, bounce it, then split and re-cluster the chops with a seed generator at 16 voices, repeating at 1/16 for a second clip.
Prepare harmonic mixes by running tracks through key-detection software and carrying that key information into Rekordbox for DJ sets.
Give an unused audio loop a second life by grouping it, duplicating and bouncing the group, converting it to mono, then converting its harmony to a new MIDI track and rearranging from those notes.

Build a dynamic bass in a wavetable synth from an analog-style saw wave plus pink noise FM, with an envelope modulating the filter cutoff, velocity controlling filter decay, and multiband upward compression to lift level without squashing dynamics.
Apply a stutter effect in a track in the style popularized by Fred Again-style productions, chopping the audio rhythmically as a featured effect.
Fatten a sound by layering a sub bass under a filtered saw, leaving room for further processing to beef it up.
Run sharp-transient sounds such as a snare hitting with a kick through a soft clipper, raising gain for body and tone while keeping headroom intact.
Pull up the DAW browser with its search hotkey, load a heavy compressor preset onto a return track, and send a few decibels of any synth or instrument there for extra energy.
Print a small amount of reverb and delay into a vocal before further processing so the ambience is baked into the sound from the start.
Control two plugin parameters at once with a single XY pad, assigning one parameter to each axis, for example speed on X and amount on Y.

On a DJ controller, switch to wide tempo mode, hold shift while slowing the pitch, then sync to move a track from 130 to 85 BPM, which doubles the other track's effective tempo and speeds up its vocal.
Build a thick gliding synth in a wavetable synth by setting up the MIDI glide behavior, shaping the synth parameters, and finishing with effects and automation.

Make basslines move by driving a synth filter's cutoff with automation toggled on and off and stacking parallel, erosion, and double-erosion effects for a deep rhythmic groove in a Summit, Dom Dolla, and Odd Mob style.
Draw chords in Ableton with an alternative method to the usual note-by-note entry, speeding up chord writing.

Turn CDJs into playable synths by setting a very short loop, tightening it with the loop-out control and jog wheel, switching master tempo off and pitch range to wide, tuning the loop with the pitch fader, and shaping it with a bandpass sweep effect.

Build a live loop mix on a DJ controller by syncing and playing the first deck, taking a two-bar auto loop, bringing the second track's fader up, syncing and playing it, adding a quarter-beat transform effect, then dropping the first track out.

Generate new melodies from an existing one by duplicating the track, opening the MIDI editor's recombine function on shuffle, transforming it into randomized variations, then transposing the result up an octave for a counter-melody.

Speed up Ableton sessions by inserting a chord with a hold-plus-arrow shortcut, prefixing track names with a hashtag for automatic numbering, and using hot-swap mode to replace one sample across a whole section at once.
Isolate vocals or instruments on a DJ controller using the stems feature in Rekordbox, set up for decks like the FLX4.
Find fresh sample material by entering a favorite song into a similar-songs finder site, which returns hundreds of lesser-known tracks in the same vein.
Remix a classic into tech house by splitting its vocals from the instrumental with a stem-separation tool, importing and processing the isolated vocal, then adding new drums and a bassline.
Design a deep rhythmic sub bass with a multipass instrument rack, phase distortion, and a frequency shifter moved from 220 Hz up to 418 Hz.

Reshape sounds at the harmonic level by editing individual harmonics by hand, shifting the formant of several harmonics at once, and resynthesizing audio into new sounds including watery vocoder textures.
Dial in an AutoTune vocal chain in FL Studio in the style of Travis Scott's tuned vocal sound.
Source acapellas for sampling by searching a short phrase on short-form video feeds, then bring the found vocals into a hardware sampling workflow.
Turn a plain plucked melody into a scratchy vibrato line with no plugins by shaping an LFO and enabling grace-note ornaments with tuned amount and velocity.
Create a swelling pad in Ableton by side-chaining its reverb so the pad breathes around the beat, tuned with pitch, reverb, and EQ adjustments.
Layer a tech house drum beat step by step from the main percussion groove, adding off-beat hats, a clap, a groove tom, and finally the kick.
